blocks.title: 1. Solving for Principal (P)

explanation: When the interest amount, rate, and time are known, we can find the principal by rearranging the simple interest formula.
From $I = P \times R \times T$, solve for $P$: $$P = \frac{I}{R \times T}$$.
Make sure $R$ is in decimal form and $T$ is in years.
This is useful when you know the interest cost and want to determine the original loan amount.
[[imp:Always convert the rate to decimal and time to years before substituting into the formula.]]

notes: $T$ = time in years; months ÷ 12, days ÷ 360 or 365.

blocks.title: 4. Solving for Any Unknown Using the Formula

notes: All $R$ values are annual rates in decimal; all $T$ values in years.
Convert $T$ from years to months/days as required.
formulaCard.title: Simple Interest Unknowns
formulaCard.formula: $$I = P \times R \times T$$ $$P = \frac{I}{R \times T}$$ $$R = \frac{I}{P \times T}$$ $$T = \frac{I}{P \times R}$$

explanation: The simple interest formula can be rearranged to solve for any of the four variables: $I$, $P$, $R$, $T$.
Choose the correct form based on the knowns:
- Unknown $P$: $$P = \frac{I}{R \times T}$$.
- Unknown $R$: $$R = \frac{I}{P \times T}$$.
- Unknown $T$: $$T = \frac{I}{P \times R}$$.
Always ensure the units of time match the interest method (ordinary/exact) and express the final answer in the requested unit.
[[imp:Memorize the base formula $I = PRT$ — the others follow by simple algebra.]]

formulaCard.title: Blueprint for Unknowns
notes: Write down the given numbers with labels.
Plug into the correct formula; don't mix up formulas.
formulaCard.formula: $$\text{Step 1: Identify knowns and unknown.}$$ $$\text{Step 2: Choose } P = \frac{I}{R \times T}, R = \frac{I}{P \times T}, T = \frac{I}{P \times R}$$ $$\text{Step 3: Check with } I = P \times R \times T$$

explanation: Use the three‑step blueprint for any simple interest unknown problem:
1. Understand: list P, R, I, T as given; identify which one is missing.
2. Solve: select the correct formula ($P = I/(R×T)$, $R = I/(P×T)$, or $T = I/(P×R)$) and compute.
3. Conclude: verify your answer by substituting it back into $I = P \times R \times T$ to ensure consistency.
This structured approach eliminates guesswork.
